head: tin
rule: Only four words were open here, and they file plainly: สุดตีน, ขี้ตีน and กวนตีน are the literal foot (sense 1), and ตีนผี, the timber beneath a roof's หางหงส์, is the lower part of a made thing (sense 2). The rule that matters on this head is one I cannot apply, because it concerns compounds already filed. **Sense 3 is glossed with two bare synonyms, ชาย, เชิง — an edge or hem — and it has become a magnet holding seven words that are not edges at all**: ถุงตีน is a sock, ฝีตีน is a pace, ตีนแมว is a burglar, ตีนโท is elephantiasis, ปลายตีน is the foot-end of a sleeper — all the literal foot, sense 1 — while ตีนคู้ and ตีนเหยียด are the ◌ู and ◌ุ vowel marks, named for a foot's shape, which is sense 2. Meanwhile the ONE word whose own gloss says เชิงซิ่น, ตีนจก, sits in sense 2. The sense list is exactly inverted, and every one of the eight was placed by gloss similarity.
